title: KCSAT-ML: Probing Reasoning Models with Nationwide-Cohort Human Difficulty

live_model.evidence: Sec. 3.2: 'Predictions are scored with an LLM-based equivalence judge (GPT-5-2025-08-07)'; Table 8: 'GPT-5 (High) ✓ 6,442 94.1' (Avg.Tok, Score); 'GPT-5 (Minimal) 8 7.7'

prompt.location: Appendix Figure 13 'Prompt templates used in experiments' (VLM and LLM settings, wo./w. TTS, judge prompt)
prompt.note: VLMs receive the problem image, LLMs the OCR text; short-answer format

claim.metric: accuracy (%) on KCSAT-ML core items, GPT-5 with high reasoning effort
claim.location: Appendix Table 8, row GPT-5 (High), column Score (339 core items with official error rates)

data.source: KCSAT-ML (664 problems, 339 core items with cohort error rates), https://github.com/naver-ai/KCSAT-ML

notes: High-reasoning GPT-5 averages 6.4k output tokens per item, so 339 items x 3 seeds is roughly $100-200 plus judge calls. The subject 'GPT-5' snapshot is not restated in Table 8 but the paper uses gpt-5-2025-08-07 throughout; GPT-5-Mini (High) 86.1 is a cheaper alternative.
